newsitem.title: USA: San Diego stadium opponents take battle to court.
newsitem.headline: San Diego stadium opponents take battle to court.

text.p: Opponents of San Diego's plan to expand its stadium will go to court next week in a bid to freeze project construction until a special election can be held, their attorneys said Monday.
A hearing was set for Jan 29 in superior court on whether the referendum drive should apply to the entire $80-million-plus project or just to the $18 million added to the expansion plan last month.
Attorneys representing project opponents said they would argue in court next week that the $18 million additions substantially changed the original expansion agreement.

As a result of these "substantial" changes, the entire expansion project should be placed on the ballot, according to Mike Aguirre, a lawyer for the Stadium Expansion on the Ballot committee. If successful in court, he said San Diego would have to halt construction until a special election is held.
San Diego's lawyers were expected to argue in court that only the $18 million additions fell under the referendum and that the original $60 million need not appear on the ballot.
For months, San Diego's plan to expand Jack Murphy stadium has faced legal and political challenges.

The project cleared a major legal hurdle last October when California's state Supreme Court ruled against tax activists, who had challenged San Diego's bond proposal to fund the expansion. The decision cleared the way for San Diego to issue revenue bonds to help fund the project.
But opponents of the expansion responded to the court decision by mounting a new challenge -- a referendum drive to force the city council to put the issue on the ballot.
They turned in more than 50,000 signatures, far more than the amount required. The city clerk is still evaluating the referendum. The signature count should be completed by Jan 24.
The construction project got underway despite this latest challenge.
The city said the bonds for the project would be repaid with revenues generated from ticket, concession, advertising and parking revenues.
